name: Cryptic crossword No 22,696
preamble: The three unclued answers are discoverers of a kind.

clue.text: Kind of twisting hill path on Capri

indicators.note: something twisting winds and turns about, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a winding hillside track on the Italian island of Capri.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as 'sort of', introducing the path; in fact 'Kind' alone is the definition and 'of' merely joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Philanthropical means benevolent towards fellow humans, so a kind, generous person can be described this way.

clue.text: Asking to observe man in church? On the contrary!

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it
the setter flips the stated order, so the outer and inner roles are swapped from how they are first given

blocks.note: a man is a human being, split around the middle
to observe is to see
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone asks to watch a man inside a church, then the setter reverses the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the man goes inside the church; 'On the contrary!' reverses the roles, so the church and the observing go inside the man, who is split around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg or implore earnestly, so beseeching is a pleading form of asking.

clue.text: Cites, perhaps, in account of person living austerely

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the word given is only one possible arrangement of its letters
one thing set in another sits inside it

blocks.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account
taken as written

explanation.surface: A biographer quotes sources in a life story of a hermit-like figure.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is the bookkeeping abbreviation for account; the rearranged letters sit between its two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic renounces comfort and pleasure, practising severe self-discipline, often for religious reasons.

clue.text: Fix exact position

blocks.note: first meaning: a predicament, as in 'in a tight corner'
second meaning: a precise place or location

explanation.surface: An instruction to pin down a precise location, as on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like a verb meaning to locate, but it is the noun sense of a difficult situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tight place is a predicament, and the same word names a particular place or point.

clue.text: Object to power showing signs of unpleasantness

definitions.note: loosely, the quality itself rather than its outward signs

blocks.note: to object is to disagree
joins the two pieces
power in the sense of capacity or ability

explanation.surface: Someone protests against authority and displays bad temper in doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to protest; 'to' simply joins it to the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreeability is the quality of being unfriendly, bad-tempered or awkward to deal with.

clue.text: Second themes in fugues could be bar-room topics

blocks.note: first meaning: a musical term for the secondary melody set against the main subject
second meaning, read in two parts: things talked about across a pub's serving bar

explanation.surface: Musical jargon about fugues might be what drinkers chat about in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word: the counter is the bar in a pub, and subjects are topics of conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fugue, a contrapuntal secondary melody accompanying the main theme is the technical name used here.

clue.text: People with arms, which move rapidly along the ground

definitions.text: which move rapidly along the ground

blocks.note: first meaning: people carrying firearms

blocks.clueFragment: which move rapidly along the ground
blocks.note: second meaning: in cricket, balls that skid low after pitching instead of bouncing

explanation.surface: Armed people, perhaps soldiers, advancing quickly across terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' suggests limbs, but means weapons; the second sense is a cricket term for a delivery that stays very low, skimming along the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunmen are those who fire weapons, and cricket uses the same word for low-skidding deliveries.

clue.text: Vehicle with runner left in southern limit

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
L is the abbreviation for left
a limit is a boundary or edge

explanation.surface: A vehicle and its driver abandoned at the far southern boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete or a messenger, but belongs to the definition: the runners are the blades a sledge glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge is a vehicle that travels over snow on long narrow blades rather than wheels.

clue.text: Takes the "Express"?

blocks.note: surface reading: buys or reads the Daily Express newspaper
setter's reading: boards an express railway service

explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British newspaper, so 'takes the Express' sounds like subscribing to it; an express is also a fast train.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to get on board a railway carriage, the opposite of alighting or detraining.

clue.text: Worker at end of leave gets advance payment

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An employee coming back from holiday receives an advance on wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' in crosswords very often means an ant or a bee.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker an ante is the stake each player puts in before the cards are dealt, paid up front.

clue.text: Chess rival I overturned, lacking small courtesies

indicators.note: an overturned board scatters the pieces, so the letters land in a new arrangement
to be lacking something is to be without it, so it is taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, and one S is removed

explanation.surface: A chess player tips over the board, showing poor manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder has two Ss; dropping one leaves exactly the ten letters needed. 'lacking small courtesies' reads as a phrase but splits after 'small'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalries are gallant acts of politeness and consideration, especially the old-fashioned gestures of a gentleman.

clue.text: Mood shown by doctor with specialisation

blocks.note: by and at both mean next to, as in 'by the door'
MO is a medical officer, a doctor
a sphere is a field of expertise or activity

explanation.surface: A doctor's bedside manner reflects his particular field.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, medical officer, is a common crossword doctor; 'by' looks like a link word but supplies a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere of a place or occasion is its prevailing feeling or tone, its general mood.

clue.text: Drunkenly, I echo "The Queen" in a toast

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of order, so the letters are jumbled
one thing set in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A tipsy guest repeats 'The Queen' as the loyal toast is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina; the loyal toast to the monarch is a British dinner tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British drinking salutation, like 'cheers', said when raising glasses.

clue.text: Great people accommodated in dilapidated semi?

indicators.note: a dilapidated building has fallen apart, so its letters are in disarray
to be accommodated in somewhere is to be housed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
men are people

explanation.surface: Important figures are found living in a run-down house.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a semi-detached house, a British staple sharing one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means huge or vast in size or degree, which is a sense of great.

clue.text: Enthusiast to follow pigeon

blocks.note: an enthusiast is a fan
to tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sets out to track a pigeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' looks like an instruction to place one piece after another, but it supplies a verb synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The fantail is a domestic breed of pigeon with a spread, fan-shaped tail.

clue.text: North Sea rowing unsettled these people

indicators.note: unsettled things are thrown out of their places, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for North
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choppy rowing on the North Sea unnerved a boatload of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these people' is a definition by context: Norway borders the North Sea, and its seafaring people fit the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwegians are the nation of Norway, Scandinavian neighbours across the water from Britain.

clue.text: Ruth, born at Lincoln?

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for born
Abraham Lincoln was known as Abe

explanation.surface: Someone called Ruth was born in the English city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the cathedral city in England, but is the US president; Ruth is the American baseball star.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe was the nickname of George Herman Ruth, the famous New York Yankees baseball player.

clue.text: Get down to remove picture from setting?

blocks.note: first meaning: to climb off a horse or bicycle
second meaning: take a picture off its backing or frame

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb down and take a picture out of its frame.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word literally: a mount is the card or frame a picture is set in, so 'dis-' takes it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders alight from a horse this way, and framers detach artwork from its backing board likewise.

clue.text: Bone with a little useful name

indicators.note: only a small part of the following text is wanted, a piece lying inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A bone with a handy label, as in an anatomy lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' looks like a quantity of usefulness, but it signals that a small piece of the next words is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the human forearm, on the side opposite the thumb.

clue.text: Local returning books about State

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
to be about something is to surround it

blocks.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
to state is to aver, assert

explanation.surface: Someone from the area brings library books back concerning the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun for a nation but is the verb to declare; a local is British slang for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house, and the British call their neighbourhood pub their local.

clue.text: Bug or nettle to cause sting

blocks.note: first meaning: to annoy, both words being verbs here
second meaning: to inflame the skin and make it smart

explanation.surface: An insect or a stinging plant leaves a painful mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' and 'nettle' look like nouns, an insect and a plant, but both are verbs meaning to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To vex or annoy someone is one sense; to make skin inflamed and sore is the physical sense.
